title: Deepak Prasad: Senior Product Manager Profile & Positioning
chunk: Deepak Prasad is a Senior Product Manager with 7+ years of experience building and scaling products across SaaS, conversational AI, B2B marketplaces, consumer subscriptions, connected hardware, and workflow automation. He specializes in 0→1 discovery from ambiguous charters, turning physical and operational bottlenecks into scalable digital platforms across B2B and B2C ecosystems.

title: Education: Bachelor of Engineering (B.E.) from VTU (2018)
chunk: Deepak Prasad holds a Bachelor of Engineering (B.E.) from Visvesvaraya Technological University (VTU), graduating in 2018 with a technical foundation in systems engineering, signal processing, and computing.

title: Complete Career History & Chronological Timeline
chunk: Deepak's verified career chronology comprises five roles: 1) Associate Product Manager at LionCircuits (Jul 2018 – May 2020), 2) Product Manager at ReshaMandi (Jun 2021 – Sep 2023), 3) Product Manager at Sportstech (Aug 2023 – Sep 2024), 4) Senior Product Manager at Sportstech (Oct 2024 – May 2026), and 5) Product Consultant | Independent via Tejmonvi Softwares (May 2026 – Jul 2026). title: ReshaMandi Thesis & Ground Field Research
chunk: The foundational thesis of ReshaMandi was: 'The product wasn't the app. The workflow was.' Field research in Ramanagara and Sidlaghatta mandis revealed an informal operational web running on 'Notebook → Photo → WhatsApp → Call'. Farmers arrived early with perishable crates in bright sunlight; requiring them to use a complex self-serve smartphone app failed. Deepak chose an assisted model: placing digital tools in the hands of trained collection centre staff while farmers received instant SMS confirmations.

title: ReshaMandi Instant Payout Engine & Settlement Rails
chunk: At ReshaMandi, Deepak owned the instant-payout workflow integrating Razorpay banking rails and internal accounting systems: transactions under ₹5L settled immediately upon lot weighing and quality confirmation, while amounts over ₹5L cleared within 2 hours. Payout reliability reached 99.9%, as monthly disbursement volume scaled from ~₹10–15 Cr to ₹20–25 Cr across 80,000+ farmers on a ₹2,000 Cr platform, eliminating predatory middlemen credit cycles.

title: Jagr: Autonomous Context Reconstruction Engine for PMs
chunk: Jagr is Deepak's flagship AI system built around the problem: 'Knowing what changed while I was away.' When product managers step away from Slack, GitHub, Linear, and Jira, context fractures across hundreds of messages, PRs, and tickets. Jagr continuously ingests team signals and operates on a 5-step loop: CONNECT → WATCH → INVESTIGATE → DECIDE → BRIEF. It strips noise, separates evidence into Observed vs Inferred vs Unknown, detects scope drift, and synthesizes an executive morning delta briefing with action items requiring PM sign-off. Throughout, human PM approval boundaries are enforced.

source: AI Systems I Built — Product Jury
title: Product Jury: Decision System for Product Managers
chunk: Product Jury is an applied AI system designed by Deepak based on the thesis: 'Make a product call you can defend — and keep the defence.' It solves the problem of product decisions vanishing after meetings. The system turns product judgements into permanent, defensible decision records through an 11-step loop: Artifact → Evidence → Jury → Decision → Red Team → Record → Revisit. It convenes multi-perspective evidence-aware jury personas and subjects provisional verdicts to red-team challenge. Crucially, the human PM always decides; the system never issues instructions.

source: AI Systems I Built — Dīpa Architecture
title: Dīpa: In-Memory Vectorless RAG Portfolio Assistant
chunk: Dīpa is the AI assistant running directly on Deepak's portfolio website. It uses an in-memory vectorless RAG architecture: build-time dense vector generation using gemini-embedding-2-preview (512-dim), in-memory exact cosine similarity ranking on server startup (zero hosted vector database latency or cost), a strict 0.68 confidence threshold for honest abstention, and constrained synthesis via gemini-3.1-flash-lite strictly citing retrieved source chunks without external hallucinations.

title: Why RAG Over Fine-Tuning for Portfolio Knowledge
chunk: Parametric weights in fine-tuned models are lossy and stochastic. When asked for precise historical metrics (such as ReshaMandi's ₹20–25 Cr monthly escrow disbursement or VTU engineering credentials), fine-tuned models frequently hallucinate plausible-sounding errors. In contrast, RAG cleanly separates knowledge storage from reasoning, guaranteeing 100% factual fidelity, instant updates without re-training, and verifiable citation provenance.

title: Dīpa Grounding Contract & Difference Between Fact and Absence of Fact
chunk: Dīpa operates under strict epistemic rules: it only answers from verified portfolio and resume evidence. If a fact is supported, it cites the source. If asked about facts not in the portfolio or resume, it clearly states: 'I don't have that in Deepak's verified portfolio material' rather than guessing. It distinguishes between fact and absence of fact: for example, LionCircuits is recognized as his earliest listed role, but not assumed to be his first job ever unless specified. For unlisted timeframes (like May 2020 – Jun 2021), it assumes nothing.

title: Cocoon Bidding System: Real-Time Bidding Mechanics
chunk: Deepak's cocoon bidding system replaced subjective buyer-seller bargaining with a digital auction mechanism. The workflow: farmers' cocoon crates were weighed on digital scales and assigned a QR lot tag (Scan); reelers placed sealed bids or competed in dynamic windows (Bid); prices updated on mobile and mandi displays (Watch); highest bidder won the lot (Win); and payment triggered immediately to the farmer via instant banking rails (Pay). Transaction value improved >35% over manual baseline.

source: Behind the AI Copilot: Voice & Indian Languages
title: Voice Mode & Indian Language Localization via Sarvam AI Proxy
chunk: Dīpa features an optional "Talk to Dīpa in your language" voice mode supporting English, Hindi (हिन्दी), Kannada (ಕನ್ನಡ), Tamil (தமிழ்), and Telugu (తెలుగు) powered by Sarvam AI. The end-to-end voice pipeline operates as follows: 1) Browser audio recording via MediaRecorder (auto-selecting Opus/WebM or MP4 with a 29-second hard stop); 2) Audio uploaded as-is to a dedicated Cloudflare Worker proxy (/stt) for Sarvam speech-to-text; 3) If non-English, the transcript is translated to English via Sarvam (/translate); 4) The English question queries the existing in-memory Gemini RAG pipeline in concise voice mode (<= 3 sentences, ~500 characters); 5) If non-English, the answer is translated back to the visitor's language via Sarvam (/translate) with speaker_gender set to "male"; 6) The translated answer is synthesized to MP3 audio via Sarvam (/tts) on user play. The Sarvam API key resides securely inside the Cloudflare Worker proxy, never exposed to client browsers, enforcing per-visitor (15 requests/day) and site-wide (300/day) limits and origin verification. Any service limit, network failure, or unauthorized origin triggers graceful fallback to standard text chat with friendly explanations. Grammatically, Hindi marks gender on verbs and pronouns; the proxy specifies male speaker gender to align with the male TTS voice persona and prevent default feminine inflection.

source: Behind the AI Copilot: Building on Sarvam AI
title: Building on Sarvam AI: PM Field Notes & Lessons
chunk: When building Dīpa's voice and Indian language support on Sarvam AI, Deepak documented four key PM field notes and engineering lessons: 1) Browser audio MIME rejection: Chrome records as 'audio/webm;codecs=opus', which Sarvam's speech-to-text API rejected with 'Invalid file type'; Deepak normalized content types in the Cloudflare Worker proxy so Chrome and Safari recordings succeed. 2) Grammatical gender in translation: Default Hindi translation picked feminine forms (आप कैसी हैं?); setting speaker_gender to 'male' aligned both speaker and addressee forms with Sarvam's male TTS voice persona (bulbul:v3). 3) Pricing consistency: Public pricing and API docs cited conflicting translation rates (₹0.005/char vs ₹20/10k chars); Deepak recommends unified rate documentation and cost estimators. 4) Designing for a prepaid wallet: Sarvam's docs say API calls fail outright once the prepaid balance reaches zero. I haven't hit that in production; I designed for it up front. Deepak implemented proxy-side limits, a per-visitor and daily cap, and a friendly 'Voice is resting' fallback to text. Suggestion: low-balance alerts by email or WhatsApp and a small grace buffer for paying accounts. Architecture: Browser recording → Cloudflare Worker proxy → Sarvam STT (saaras:v3) → Sarvam translate (sarvam-translate:v1) → Gemini RAG, unchanged → translation back → Sarvam TTS (bulbul:v3). Result: voice works end to end in Chrome and Safari across English, Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, and Telugu. A typical voice round trip takes about 3-4 seconds. Next: measure which languages visitors actually choose, and test whether voice changes how many questions they ask.
